real_postgres_tests.TestTransferInstanceOwnerIsOneAtomicSwap: the marker moves, exactly one row holds it, the former owner keeps admin, and every ineligible target (ordinary user, unknown id, deactivated admin, tombstoned admin) changes nothing — including the clear, which carries the same test
real_postgres_tests.TestConcurrentOwnerTransfersCannotBothWi: two transfers to DIFFERENT admins, interleaved deliberately: the second blocks on the first's uncommitted marker, and when the first commits the second is refused by users_single_owner_idx with SQLSTATE 23505 (mapped to 409 owner_transfer_conflict). One winner, one marked account. Firing both from goroutines proves nothing — they serialize and both legitimately succeed in order, which is why the test forces the interleaving.

sc5_last_admin_race.why: the guard has FOUR write paths (admin PATCH, self-deactivate, self-delete, admin hard delete) and they only serialize against each other if they share ONE lock, which means the count and the write must sit in the same transaction. Two are a single UPDATE and could carry a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE roster lock in-statement; the hard delete cannot — it is a multi-table erasure that also deletes blobs and fans a federation Delete out, and holding a roster lock across that is worse than the race. A partial fold buys almost nothing, because a mixed race (one admin PATCHing while the other self-deletes) stays open unless every path takes the lock. The real fix is a transaction seam threaded through admin, auth and account together: structural, not surgical.
sc5_last_admin_race.where: the reason now lives on internal/admin/service.go ensureAdminRemains rather than in a report
